Here’s why many people find the evidence convincing:

India’s ISRO, the European Space Agency (ESA), and others have orbited Mars – not with any US or Russian “script” to follow – and have taken extremely high-resolution photos of the landing sites. These images show not just the rovers themselves, but their tracks, discarded parachutes, and heat shields. These countries have their own scientific agendas, their own engineers, and their own national pride. France, Germany, Italy, Japan, and India all have nothing to gain by perpetuating a lie for NASA’s benefit – quite the opposite; they’d gain enormous prestige by exposing a hoax. The fact that multiple independent orbiters see the same hardware in the same spots is a strong cross-check.

The rovers on Mars don’t just send pictures to NASA; they broadcast radio signals that anyone on Earth can, in principle, detect with a large enough dish. Amateur radio astronomers and universities worldwide have tracked the spacecraft and received data directly. You can even pick up the faint signals from Mars orbiters and sometimes surface assets using hobbyist equipment or open-source software like GNU Radio. These signals come from a specific moving point on Mars, consistent with a rover on the surface, not from an Earth-bound simulator. If it were all faked, the entire international deep-space network would have to be in on it.

Martian meteorites, the planet’s atmosphere, and the rover’s chemical analyses all agree with each other. For example, the study of Mars’ surface composition from orbit matches what the rovers find in their spectrometers. Hundreds of universities in dozens of countries – including those with no connection to the US government – crunch this data, publish peer-reviewed papers, and build careers on it. When the Soviet Venera landers touched down on Venus, they sent back pictures of a harsh, yellow-orange landscape under crushing pressure and 900°F heat. When a rover talks to Earth, it emits radio waves through deep space.
